Guarantees: Operations appear instantaneous in a real-time order; reads see latest committed write
Use Case: Coordination services (locks, leader election), strongly-consistent KV
Weaknesses: Lower availability under partition; higher latency (consensus round-trips)
Notes: Provided by etcd, ZooKeeper, Spanner, FoundationDB. Most expensive guarantee.

Guarantees: All clients see operations in the same order, not necessarily real-time
Notes: Often confused with linearizability — sequential drops the real-time constraint.

Guarantees: Causally-related operations seen in causal order; concurrent ops can differ
Use Case: Collaborative apps, social feeds, distributed databases (Cosmos DB)
Weaknesses: Implementation needs causal metadata (vector clocks, dependencies)
Notes: Cosmos DB's 'Session' consistency is essentially causal+'monotonic reads' for that session.

Guarantees: You see your own writes; reads never go back in time within a session
Algorithms: Session token routed to primary or to replicas with sufficient replay
Notes: Implement via 'last-write LSN' cookie or session-pinned routing.

Guarantees: All replicas converge if writes stop
Notes: Acceptable for analytics, recommendations, notifications. Pair with conflict resolution (LWW/CRDT).

Guarantees: Concurrent updates always converge to the same value without coordination
Use Case: Collaborative editing, distributed counters, presence, offline-first apps
Weaknesses: Limited operation set; data structures non-trivial
Notes: Yjs and Automerge are the production-grade JS/Rust libs (Liveblocks, Jupyter, Linear).

Guarantees: Under network partition, choose Consistency or Availability
Use Case: Mental model for distributed DB choice
Weaknesses: Often misquoted (P is not optional in real systems)
Notes: Modern framing: PACELC — 'else, latency vs consistency' even without partition.

Guarantees: Even without partition, trade off latency vs consistency
Notes: Daniel Abadi's extension. Spanner = PC/EC, DynamoDB default = PA/EL.

Weaknesses: Throughput limited by leader; partition halves cluster
Notes: Raft is the practical choice for new systems; etcd/raft is the most-used Go impl.
Spanner & Chubby use Paxos variants; new code almost always picks Raft instead.

Weaknesses: Blocking on coordinator failure; poor latency
Notes: Avoid in microservices — use Saga + Outbox + idempotency instead.

Guarantees: Reads see consistent snapshot; writes detect conflicts (SSI = serializable)
Use Case: Postgres (REPEATABLE READ → SSI via SERIALIZABLE), CockroachDB
Strengths: No read locks; SSI gives true serializability
Weaknesses: Write skew (in non-SSI snapshot); retry-on-conflict UX
Notes: Postgres 'SERIALIZABLE' uses SSI; expect serialization failures and retry idempotently.

Guarantees: Configurable consistency vs availability per op
Weaknesses: Misconfiguration leads to data loss / stale reads
Notes: Cassandra default LOCAL_QUORUM gives intra-DC strong consistency.
Used internally by Riak, Cassandra hinted handoff, CRDT libraries.

Guarantees: Combines physical + logical clock; bounded skew
Strengths: Better than pure logical for human-readable timestamps
Notes: Used by CockroachDB, YugabyteDB. Spanner's TrueTime is a stronger (HW-backed) alternative.
